purpose: Record exact current public source owners, types, intended GCRB adapter direction, and boundaries that prevent duplicated or overclaimed state.

adapters.intended_gcrb_use: Use typed Case/Evidence/Decision/Appeal references when a human-authorized dispute or appeal is actually opened under the appropriate policy and jurisdiction. GCRB may submit an anomaly/contest packet to a qualified review path; it must not open punitive cases or infer guilt automatically.
boundaries: An anomaly is a review lead, not a finding of misconduct.
A Decision or Appeal record proves only that the relevant record exists under that hApp's validation rules; it does not establish truth outside its documented evidence and authority.
Do not duplicate the Justice Cases lifecycle or create parallel case/appeal state in Symthaea.
Validate case IDs, evidence references, appeal deadlines, and visibility/privacy policy through the owner API; this adapter is not implemented.

adapters.owner_class: domain-specific signed event and transparency pattern
adapters.intended_gcrb_use: Reuse the documented architectural pattern—domain-separated canonical event envelope, monotonically sequenced hash chain, receipt-time acceptance signature, and witnessed transparency checkpoint—when designing a dedicated GCRB/civic evidence event profile.
boundaries: CredentialGovernanceEnvelope and CredentialGovernancePayload are credential-specific; do not insert civic allegations or public policy events into credential semantics.

Acceptance signature, receipt time, chain continuity, and Merkle roots prove defined integrity/currentness properties only when their verifier and trust roots are qualified; they do not prove an event's real-world truth.
A civic event profile must define its own actor roles, authorization rules, evidence classes, retention/privacy policy, and type versioning.
No runtime GCRB adapter or trusted recorder is implemented.

adapters.intended_gcrb_use: Consume simulation results through a read-only adapter that stores the exact input-manifest digest, simulator commit/build ID, scenario/config hash, seed, tick/time horizon, output digest, uncertainty/limitations, and evidence class 'simulated'. Compare to independently observed outcomes only in a separate measurement adapter.
boundaries: SimSnapshot and SimEvent are transient transport structures in the inspected public source and do not themselves establish a durable, authenticated evidence record.
Do not label a simulated outcome as observed, predicted-as-calibrated, or policy-validated without a separate claim-specific evaluation.
Do not duplicate Symtropy's physics, scenario, or governance simulation state machine in the GCRB evaluator.
The GCRB adapter is not implemented.

adapters.intended_gcrb_use: Potential future adapter if the standalone build/dependency publication boundary is resolved and exact simulation inputs/outputs can be pinned.
boundaries: The standalone Symtropy Cargo.toml explicitly comments that this bridge is not wired as a dependency in the default workspace because its simulation bridge and Mycelix dependencies are unpublished/stripped.
Source presence is not evidence of a runnable cross-repository integration.
Do not claim Symtropy and Mycelix are currently interoperating through this bridge.
Do not enable a hidden or private dependency as a shortcut to qualification.

cross_system_invariants: GCRB never creates a parallel Mycelix case, evidence, decision, or appeal ledger.
GCRB does not reuse credential-specific Mycelix event payloads as civic semantics.
Symtropy output remains typed as simulated until independently corroborated.
Every future adapter pins exact source/build/schema digests and records unknown/missing evidence instead of imputing zero or success.
No cross-system runtime integration, source authority verification, or production qualification is claimed by this map.
